proof:
The zero-mass case is immediate. For each affine $A$ define on $U$ the signed measure $B\mapsto\int\mathbf1_B(u)A(x)\,d(\eta-\nu)$. It vanishes because it integrates every continuous test to zero. For each convex $\Phi$ the analogous signed measure with integrand $\Phi(x)$ is nonnegative, since its integral against every nonnegative continuous test is nonnegative. Thus for every Borel $B\subset U$, the restrictions of $\nu,\eta$ to $B\times X$ have physical marginals in equal-mass convex order. This uses the affine constant test for equal mass and does not require choosing exceptional parameter sets for individual tests.

For $\delta>0$, use a finite Borel partition of $U$ of mesh at most $\delta$, obtained by successively removing earlier balls from a finite cover by balls of radius $\delta/2$. Apply the compact physical martingale lemma to each cell's two physical marginals. Lift each coupling by $(x,y)\mapsto((n(x),x),(n(y),y))$. Each lifted marginal is the prescribed marked restriction, because that restriction is concentrated on the graph of $n$. The coupling is carried by $N\times N$ and the row moment identity holds with $f(n(x),x)$, using a bounded Borel extension of $f$ by zero off $N$. Both parameters lie in the same cell almost everywhere. Sum over the cells and take a weak subsequential limit on $N\times N$ as $\delta\downarrow0$. The marginals are unchanged and the integral of the continuous parameter distance is at most $\delta$ times the common mass before the limit. It is zero in the limit. The row identities pass for continuous tests. For each coordinate, uniqueness of a finite signed measure from its continuous integrals on $N$ gives the identities for all bounded Borel tests.

For the converse, a finite coupling on compact metric spaces has regular conditional probability rows over its first coordinate whenever its mass is positive. The identities for all bounded Borel $f$ imply the coordinatewise row mean $x$ almost everywhere. Likewise $u=v$ almost everywhere implies equality of the parameters almost surely within almost every row. Affine equality and Jensen in each row, multiplied by the respective input parameter tests and integrated, give the two localized tests.

For the finite-family application, take nonempty finite $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ and compact convex bodies $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ of positive volume, $d\ge1$. Use the physical variable $w=(p,x)$ and the marked exposed-face relation $N=\{(u,p,x):u\in\mathbb S^{d-1},\ p\in P,\ x\in K_p,\ u\cdot x=h_p(u)\}$, with $h_p(u)=\max_{y\in K_p}u\cdot y$. It is compact by continuity of the support functions. In $d\ge2$ the boundary of a positive-volume convex body has local Lipschitz graph charts. At points of differentiability of the graphs the outer unit normal is unique, so Rademacher's theorem and the Lipschitz area bound give a surface-null nonregular locus and finite surface measure. More explicitly, the outer-normal multifunction on the boundary has nonempty compact values and closed graph. The subset where two normals are separated by at least $1/m$ is the projection of a compact set, hence is closed. The nonregular set is the union of these subsets over positive integers $m$, so the regular locus is Borel. The normal is continuous relative to that locus by closedness of the graph, compactness of the unit sphere, and uniqueness of the normal there. For $d=1$ the two endpoints have unique normals $-1,1$ and counting measure. Extend the normal arbitrarily and Borelly off the regular locus. The sum of the marked surface measures and any finite nonnegative measure absolutely continuous with respect to that sum are then supported on the same Borel graph in $N$. The lemma gives exact normal equality and the full physical mean. For almost every input $(u,p,x)$, disintegrate the coupling and let $\alpha_q$ be its probability of output base $q$. The base part of the mean gives $\sum_q\alpha_q q=p$. Every output $(u,q,y)$ satisfies $u\cdot y=h_q(u)$, and the continuous part of the mean gives $\sum_q\alpha_q h_q(u)=u\cdot x=h_p(u)$.
statement:
Let $U$ be a compact metric space, $X\subset\mathbb R^k$ compact, and $N\subset U\times X$ compact. Let $\nu,\eta$ be finite nonnegative Borel measures on $N$, both concentrated on the graph of the same Borel map $x\mapsto n(x)\in U$. Suppose
$$
\int \psi(u)A(x)\,d(\eta-\nu)(u,x)=0,\qquad
\int \psi_+(u)\Phi(x)\,d(\eta-\nu)(u,x)\ge0
$$
for every continuous $\psi$ and every nonnegative continuous $\psi_+$ on $U$, every affine $A$ on $\mathbb R^k$, and every finite continuous convex $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^k$. These conditions are equivalent to the existence of a coupling $\Pi$ from $\nu$ to $\eta$ on $N\times N$ satisfying
$$
u=v\quad\Pi\text{-a.e.},\qquad
\int f(u,x)(y-x)\,d\Pi((u,x),(v,y))=0
$$
for every bounded Borel scalar $f$ on $N$.
title: Localized convex order and exact parameter preservation
